reviews.body: Fix looks good! Only ask is a test for the partial case where one count is missing.

review_comments.body: Can we add a case where only `prompt_eval_count` is None (e.g. `eval_count=100`)? That partial case is what actually blew up the sum, and AFAIK it is the one users hit in practice. Ideally, parametrizing this test over a few combinations would be most robust.

**Suggestion** (optional): This test and `test_format_chunk_metadata` right above it have the same body; the only difference is the inputs. Per `docs/TESTING.md` ("prefer adding assertions to an existing test", "parametrize repetitive cases"), you could add the all-present case `(100, 50, 1000000, 50, 100, 1)` with id `all-present` here and delete `test_format_chunk_metadata`, so one test covers the whole metadata branch.

comments.body:
Thanks @yonib05 — added the partial cases. `test_format_chunk_metadata_missing_counts` is now parametrized over all-missing, only `prompt_eval_count` missing (`eval_count=100`), only `eval_count` missing, and only `total_duration` missing. All four fail on main with a TypeError (on the token sum, or on the duration division in the last case) and pass with the fix.
